queue.question: Does this record name the same registered substance as Dapagliflozin Propanediol? Both records carry UNII 887K2391VH. Someone needs to decide whether these records should be merged, cross-linked as alternative names for one substance, or left separate. Nothing here decides that, and no record has been changed.
queue.basis: Grouped on a shared substance identifier. 2 recorded fields match, 6 do not match, and 0 cannot be placed on one scale. Matching fields are not proof of one substance, and fields that do not match are not proof of two. Priority ranks the shared identifier signal above the shared document signal, then by how many recorded fields both records hold.

sourceReadings.label: FDA label for FARXIGA (dapagliflozin) tablets (openFDA)

sourceReadings.label: FDA label for FARXIGA (dapagliflozin) tablets (openFDA)
sourceReadings.excerpt: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), expressed in the proximal renal tubules, is responsible for the majority of the reabsorption of filtered glucose from the tubular lumen. Dapagliflozin is an inhibitor of SGLT2. By inhibiting SGLT2, dapagliflozin reduces reabsorption of filtered glucose and thereby promotes urinary glucose excretion.

sourceReadings.excerpt: The absolute oral bioavailability of dapagliflozin following the administration of a 10 mg dose is 78%.

sourceReadings.label: FDA label for FARXIGA (dapagliflozin) tablets (openFDA)
sourceReadings.excerpt: The metabolism of dapagliflozin is primarily mediated by UGT1A9; CYP-mediated metabolism is a minor clearance pathway in humans. Dapagliflozin is extensively metabolized, primarily to yield dapagliflozin 3-O-glucuronide, which is an inactive metabolite.

queue.basis: Grouped on a shared substance identifier. 1 recorded fields match, 5 do not match, and 2 cannot be placed on one scale. Matching fields are not proof of one substance, and fields that do not match are not proof of two. Priority ranks the shared identifier signal above the shared document signal, then by how many recorded fields both records hold.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Prussian blue insoluble, ferric hexacyanoferrate(II), acts by ion-exchange, adsorption, and mechanical trapping within the crystal structure, and has a high affinity for radioactive and non-radioactive cesium and thallium.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Radiogardase capsules contain insoluble ferric hexacyanoferrate(II), with an empirical formula of Fe 4 [Fe(CN) 6 ] 3 and a molecular weight of 859.3 Daltons.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Radiogardase is indicated for treatment of patients with known or suspected internal contamination with radioactive cesium and/or radioactive or non-radioactive thallium to increase their rates of elimination.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Radiogardase is indicated for treatment of patients with known or suspected internal contamination with radioactive cesium and/or radioactive or non-radioactive thallium, in order to increase their rates of elimination.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Radiogardase is not systemically bioavailable and does not rely on hepatic metabolism for activation or inactivation.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The rate of cesium and thallium elimination is proportional to the duration and dose of prussian blue insoluble.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and efficacy of Radiogardase has not been established in the treatment of 137 Cs contamination in pediatric patients 0 to 2 years old.

sourceReadings.label: Ferric Ferrocyanide label

queue.question: Does this record name the same registered substance as Adalimumab-Adaz, Adalimumab-Aqvh, Adalimumab-Atto? Both records carry UNII FYS6T7F842. Someone needs to decide whether these records should be merged, cross-linked as alternative names for one substance, or left separate. Nothing here decides that, and no record has been changed.
queue.basis: Grouped on a shared substance identifier. 4 recorded fields match, 1 do not match, and 0 cannot be placed on one scale. Matching fields are not proof of one substance, and fields that do not match are not proof of two. Priority ranks the shared identifier signal above the shared document signal, then by how many recorded fields both records hold.

sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1 , 2.2 ) in combination with carboplatin and pemetrexed for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, whose disease has progressed on or after treatment with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: 11 DESCRIPTION Amivantamab-vmjw is a low-fucose human immunoglobulin G1-based bispecific antibody directed against the EGF and MET receptors, produced by mammalian cell line (Chinese Hamster Ovary [CHO]) using recombinant DNA technology that has a molecular weight of approximately 148 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Amivantamab-vmjw is a bispecific antibody that binds to the extracellular domains of EGFR and MET.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination The mean (% CV) linear clearance (CL) is 0.26 L/day (30%) and mean terminal half-life is 14 days (33%).

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In in vitro and in vivo studies amivantamab-vmjw was able to disrupt EGFR and MET signaling functions in mutation models of exon 19 deletions, exon 21 L858R substitutions, and exon 20 insertions through blocking ligand binding or degradation of EGFR and MET.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 421 patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC treated with RYBREVANT in combination with lazertinib in the MARIPOSA study, 45% were ≥ 65 years of age and 12% were ≥ 75 years of age.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: RYBREVANT is a bispecific EGF receptor-directed and MET receptor-directed antibody indicated: in combination with lazertinib for the first-line treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on the mechanism of action and findings in animal models, RYBREVANT can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of amivantamab-vmjw in human milk, the effects on the breastfed child or on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The presence of EGFR and MET on the surface of tumor cells also allows for targeting of these cells for destruction by immune effector cells, such as natural killer cells and macrophages, through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and trogocytosis mechanisms, respectively.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and efficacy of RYBREVANT have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Treatment with amivantamab in combination with lazertinib increased in vivo anti-tumor activity compared to either agent alone in a mouse xenograft model of human NSCLC with an EGFR L858R mutation.

sourceReadings.label: Amivantamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: gs and Precautions (5.5) ] RYBREVANT in Combination with Lazertinib The most common adverse reactions (≥ 20%) were rash, nail toxicity, infusion-related reaction, musculoskeletal pain, stomatitis, edema, VTE, paresthesia, fatigue, diarrhea, constipation, COVID-19, hemorrhage, dry skin, decreased appetite, pruritus, and nausea.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Avalglucosidase alfa-ngpt provides an exogenous source of GAA.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies with NEXVIAZYME included 13 patients 65 to 74 years of age and 4 patients 75 years of age and older.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: GAA deficiency results in intralysosomal accumulation of glycogen in various tissues.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: NEXVIAZYME is a hydrolytic lysosomal glycogen-specific enzyme indicated for the treatment of patients 1 year of age and older with late-onset Pompe disease (lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase [GAA] deficiency).

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: NEXVIAZYME is indicated for the treatment of patients 1 year of age and older with late-onset Pompe disease (lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase [GAA] deficiency).

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Pompe disease (also known as glycogen storage disease type II, acid maltase deficiency, and glycogenosis type II) is an inherited disorder of glycogen metabolism caused by a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme acid α-glucosidase (GAA) that degrades glycogen to glucose in the lysosome.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of avalglucosidase alfa-ngpt in either human or animal milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The M6P on avalglucosidase alfa-ngpt mediates binding to M6P receptors on the cell surface with high affinity.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The effects of NEXVIAZYME were evaluated based on comparison with a control group treated with DPH alone.

sourceReadings.label: Avalglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Use of NEXVIAZYME for this indication is supported by evidence from two clinical studies which included adults with LOPD, and 1 pediatric patient with LOPD (16 years of age) and from safety experience in 19 pediatric patients with infantile-onset Pompe disease (IOPD) (1 to 12 years of age) treated with NEXVIAZYME [see Clinical Studies (14.1) ] .

sourceReadings.excerpt: WARNING: SEVERE HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, INFUSION-ASSOCIATED REACTIONS, and RISK OF ACUTE CARDIORESPIRATORY FAILURE IN SUSCEPTIBLE PATIENTS WARNING: SEVERE HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, INFUSION-ASSOCIATED REACTIONS, and RISK OF ACUTE CARDIORESPIRATORY FAILURE IN SUSCEPTIBLE PATIENTS See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning.

sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 ) for the adjuvant treatment of adult patients with CSCC at high risk of recurrence after surgery and radiation.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 , 14.1 ) Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic BCC (laBCC or mBCC) who have been previously treated with a hedgehog pathway inhibitor or for whom a hedgehog pathway inhibitor is not appropriate.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Binding of the PD-1 ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 to the PD-1 receptor found on T cells inhibits T-cell proliferation and cytokine production.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Cemiplimab-rwlc has an approximate molecular weight of 146 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Cemiplimab-rwlc is a recombinant human immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody that binds to PD-1 and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1 pathway-mediated inhibition of the immune response, including the anti-tumor immune response.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The volume of distribution of cemiplimab-rwlc is 5.9 L (29%).

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In syngeneic mouse tumor models, blocking PD-1 activity resulted in decreased tumor growth.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In this pooled safety population, the most common adverse reactions (≥15%) were fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, rash, diarrhea, and anemia.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LIBTAYO as a Single Agent Of the 1281 patients with advanced cancers who received LIBTAYO as a single agent in clinical studies, 26% were 65 years up to 75 years and 22% were 75 years or older.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LIBTAYO is a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) blocking antibody indicated: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (CSCC) for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (mCSCC) or locally advanced CSCC (laCSCC) who are not candidates for curative surgery or curative radiation.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on its mechanism of action, LIBTAYO can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There is no information regarding the presence of cemiplimab-rwlc in human milk, or its effects on the breastfed child or on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The elimination half-life is 22 days (42%).

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of LIBTAYO have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upregulation of PD-1 ligands occurs in some tumors and signaling through this pathway can contribute to inhibition of active T-cell immune surveillance of tumors.

sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 , 14.1 ) Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic BCC (laBCC or mBCC) who have been previously treated with a hedgehog pathway inhibitor or for whom a hedgehog pathway inhibitor is not appropriate.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Binding of the PD-1 ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 to the PD-1 receptor found on T cells inhibits T-cell proliferation and cytokine production.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Cemiplimab-rwlc has an approximate molecular weight of 146 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Cemiplimab-rwlc is a recombinant human immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody that binds to PD-1 and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1 pathway-mediated inhibition of the immune response, including the anti-tumor immune response.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The volume of distribution of cemiplimab-rwlc is 5.9 L (29%).

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In syngeneic mouse tumor models, blocking PD-1 activity resulted in decreased tumor growth.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In this pooled safety population, the most common adverse reactions (≥15%) were fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, rash, diarrhea, and anemia.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LIBTAYO as a Single Agent Of the 1281 patients with advanced cancers who received LIBTAYO as a single agent in clinical studies, 26% were 65 years up to 75 years and 22% were 75 years or older.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LIBTAYO is a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) blocking antibody indicated: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (CSCC) for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (mCSCC) or locally advanced CSCC (laCSCC) who are not candidates for curative surgery or curative radiation.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on its mechanism of action, LIBTAYO can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There is no information regarding the presence of cemiplimab-rwlc in human milk, or its effects on the breastfed child or on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The elimination half-life is 22 days (42%).

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of LIBTAYO have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Cemiplimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upregulation of PD-1 ligands occurs in some tumors and signaling through this pathway can contribute to inhibition of active T-cell immune surveillance of tumors.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The mean volume of distribution at steady state of EPA is approximately 88 liters.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Icosapent ethyl capsules are an ethyl ester of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) indicated: as an adjunct to diet to reduce TG levels in adultpatients with severe (≥ 500 mg/dL) hypertriglyceridemia.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Icosapent ethyl capsules are contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylactic reaction) to icosapent ethyl or any of its components.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Icosapent ethyl capsules are indicated: as an adjunct to diet to reduce TG levels in adult patients with severe (≥ 500 mg/dL) hypertriglyceridemia.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In patients with hepatic impairment, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels should be monitored periodically during therapy with icosapent ethyl.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Limitations of Use: The effect of icosapent ethyl capsules on the risk for pancreatitis in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia has not been determined.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the total number of patients in well-controlled clinical studies of icosapent ethyl, 45% were 65 years of age and over.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Peak plasma concentrations of EPA were reached approximately 5 hours following oral doses of icosapent ethyl.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Potential mechanisms of action include increased β-oxidation; inhibition of acyl-CoA:1,2-diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT); decreased lipogenesis in the liver; and increased plasma lipoprotein lipase activity.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Published studies have detected omega-3 fatty acids, including EPA, in human milk.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary The available data from published case reports and the pharmacovigilance database on the use of icosapent ethyl in pregnant women are insufficient to identify a drug-associated risk for major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Studies suggest that EPA reduces hepatic very low-density lipoprotein triglycerides (VLDL-TG) synthesis and/or secretion and enhances TG clearance from circulating VLDL particles.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The empirical formula of icosapent ethyl is C 22 H 34 O 2 and the molecular weight is 330.51.

sourceReadings.label: Icosapent label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The plasma elimination half-life (t1/2) of EPA is approximately 89 hours.

sourceReadings.label: Published labels naming Lerodalcibep as an active ingredient
Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Absorption The median (min, max) estimated subcutaneous bioavailability of lerodalcibep-liga is 83% (66%, 89%).

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: By inhibiting the binding of PCSK9 to LDLR, lerodalcibep-liga increases the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL-C from the blood, thereby lowering LDL-C levels. [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clearance of free lerodalcibep-liga (CV%) is 0.36 L/day (30%) with an estimated half-life of approximately 10 days.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution Lerodalcibep-liga does not extensively distribute into tissues; the apparent volume of distribution is 5.3 L.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LEROCHOL TM is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LEROCHOL is a proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise: to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Lerodalcibep-liga is a recombinant fusion protein that binds PCSK9 with picomolar affinity.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Lerodalcibep-liga is produced in genetically engineered mammalian (Chinese hamster ovary) cells as a single protein with an approximate molecular weight of 77 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dose adjustment is necessary in patients with mild (total bilirubin 1.0 to 1.5 upper limit of normal or aspartate aminotransaminase > upper limit of normal) or moderate (total bilirubin 1.5 to 3.0 upper limit of normal) hepatic impairment [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dose adjustment is necessary in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment [estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥30 to <90 mL/min] [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 1,631 patients treated with LEROCHOL 300 mg in clinical trials, 687 (42%) patients were 65 years of age and older, while 198 (12%) patients were 75 years of age or older.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: PCSK9 binds to low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) on the surface of hepatocytes to promote LDLR degradation within the liver.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Discontinue LEROCHOL when pregnancy is recognized.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of lerodalcebip-liga in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of LEROCHOL in pediatric patients have not been established.

Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Absorption The median (min, max) estimated subcutaneous bioavailability of lerodalcibep-liga is 83% (66%, 89%).

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: By inhibiting the binding of PCSK9 to LDLR, lerodalcibep-liga increases the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL-C from the blood, thereby lowering LDL-C levels. [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clearance of free lerodalcibep-liga (CV%) is 0.36 L/day (30%) with an estimated half-life of approximately 10 days.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution Lerodalcibep-liga does not extensively distribute into tissues; the apparent volume of distribution is 5.3 L.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LEROCHOL TM is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LEROCHOL is a proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise: to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Lerodalcibep-liga is a recombinant fusion protein that binds PCSK9 with picomolar affinity.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Lerodalcibep-liga is produced in genetically engineered mammalian (Chinese hamster ovary) cells as a single protein with an approximate molecular weight of 77 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dose adjustment is necessary in patients with mild (total bilirubin 1.0 to 1.5 upper limit of normal or aspartate aminotransaminase > upper limit of normal) or moderate (total bilirubin 1.5 to 3.0 upper limit of normal) hepatic impairment [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dose adjustment is necessary in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment [estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥30 to <90 mL/min] [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 1,631 patients treated with LEROCHOL 300 mg in clinical trials, 687 (42%) patients were 65 years of age and older, while 198 (12%) patients were 75 years of age or older.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: PCSK9 binds to low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) on the surface of hepatocytes to promote LDLR degradation within the liver.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Discontinue LEROCHOL when pregnancy is recognized.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of lerodalcebip-liga in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Lerodalcibep label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of LEROCHOL in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Published labels naming Lonapegsomatropin as an active ingredient
Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Hypersensitivity to somatropin or any of the excipients in SKYTROFA.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In pediatric patients with GHD, following subcutaneous dose administration of 0.24 mg/kg/week SKYTROFA, the observed mean (CV%) steady-state peak serum concentration (C max ) of lonapegsomatropin-tcgd was 1230 (86.3) ng hGH/mL, and the median time to reach maximum concentrations (T max ) was 25 hours.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Lonapegsomatropin-tcgd consists of a parent drug, somatropin, that is conjugated to a methoxypolyethylene glycol carrier (4 × 10 kDa mPEG) via a proprietary TransCon Linker and has a molecular weight of 63 kDa (released somatropin is 22 kDa).

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 249 patients who received SKYTROFA in clinical studies, 24 (10%) patients were 65 years of age and older, and 4 (2%) patients were 75 years of age and older.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Pediatric patients with closed epiphyses.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Replacement of endogenous growth hormone in adults with growth hormone deficiency (GHD).

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no available data on lonapegsomatropin-tcgd use in pregnant patients to evaluate a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of lonapegsomatropin-tcgd in human milk, effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA (lonapegsomatropin-tcgd) is a human growth hormone indicated for the: Treatment of pediatric patients 1 year and older who weigh at least 11.5 kg and have growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (GH).

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA is a human growth hormone indicated for: Pediatric Patients: Treatment of pediatric patients 1 year and older who weigh at least 11.5 kg and have growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (GH) ( 1 ).

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA is a pegylated human growth hormone (somatropin) for once-weekly subcutaneous injection [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA is contraindicated in patients with: Acute critical illness after open heart surgery, abdominal surgery or multiple accidental trauma, or those with acute respiratory failure due to the risk of increased mortality with use of pharmacologic doses of somatropin [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Severe systemic hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic reactions and angioedema, have been reported [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ].

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Somatropin binds to the growth hormone (GH) receptor in the cell membrane of target cells resulting in intracellular signal transduction and a host of pharmacodynamic effects.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Somatropin has direct tissue and metabolic effects, and indirect effects mediated by insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), including stimulation of chondrocyte differentiation and proliferation, stimulation of hepatic glucose output, protein synthesis and lipolysis.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Somatropin stimulates skeletal growth in pediatric patients with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) as a result of effects on the growth plates (epiphyses) of long bones.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The apparent half-life of somatropin released from lonapegsomatropin-tcgd was approximately 25 hours.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of SKYTROFA in children less than 1 year of age have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no available data on lonapegsomatropin-tcgd use in pregnant patients to evaluate a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA (lonapegsomatropin-tcgd) is a human growth hormone indicated for the: Treatment of pediatric patients 1 year and older who weigh at least 11.5 kg and have growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (GH).

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA is a human growth hormone indicated for: Pediatric Patients: Treatment of pediatric patients 1 year and older who weigh at least 11.5 kg and have growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (GH) ( 1 ).

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA is a pegylated human growth hormone (somatropin) for once-weekly subcutaneous injection [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SKYTROFA is contraindicated in patients with: Acute critical illness after open heart surgery, abdominal surgery or multiple accidental trauma, or those with acute respiratory failure due to the risk of increased mortality with use of pharmacologic doses of somatropin [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Severe systemic hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic reactions and angioedema, have been reported [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ].

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Somatropin binds to the growth hormone (GH) receptor in the cell membrane of target cells resulting in intracellular signal transduction and a host of pharmacodynamic effects.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Somatropin has direct tissue and metabolic effects, and indirect effects mediated by insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), including stimulation of chondrocyte differentiation and proliferation, stimulation of hepatic glucose output, protein synthesis and lipolysis.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Somatropin stimulates skeletal growth in pediatric patients with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) as a result of effects on the growth plates (epiphyses) of long bones.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The apparent half-life of somatropin released from lonapegsomatropin-tcgd was approximately 25 hours.

sourceReadings.label: Lonapegsomatropin-Tcgd label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of SKYTROFA in children less than 1 year of age have not been established.

queue.basis: Grouped on a shared substance identifier. 2 recorded fields match, 3 do not match, and 0 cannot be placed on one scale. Matching fields are not proof of one substance, and fields that do not match are not proof of two. Priority ranks the shared identifier signal above the shared document signal, then by how many recorded fields both records hold.

Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 6.1 ) Treatment of GPP Flare: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are asthenia and fatigue, headache, nausea, pruritus and prurigo, infusion site hematoma and bruising, and urinary tract infection.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: After subcutaneous administration in the abdomen, absolute bioavailability (90% CI) was slightly higher at higher doses with estimated values of 58 (51, 66)%, 65 (60, 69)%, and 72 (65, 79)% at 150 mg, 300 mg, and 600 mg, respectively.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Binding of spesolimab-sbzo to IL36R prevents the subsequent activation of IL36R by its ligands (IL-36 α, β and γ) and downstream activation of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic pathways.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies of SPEVIGO did not include sufficient numbers of subjects 65 years of age and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger adult subjects.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution Based on the population pharmacokinetic analysis, the typical total volume of distribution at steady state was 6.4 L.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Reported hypersensitivity reactions have included drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) and anaphylaxis [see Warnings and Precautions (5.3) and Adverse Reactions (6) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary The limited data on the use of SPEVIGO in pregnant women are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk of adverse pregnancy-related outcomes.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of spesolimab-sbzo in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SPEVIGO is an interleukin-36 receptor antagonist indicated for the treatment of generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older and weighing at least 40 kg.

sourceReadings.label: Spesolimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: SPEVIGO is contraindicated in patients with severe or life-threatening hypersensitivity to spesolimab-sbzo or to any of the excipients in SPEVIGO.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The total volume of distribution for tafasitamab-cxix was 9.3 L (95% CI: 8.6, 10 L).

sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination The clearance of tafasitamab-cxix was 0.41 L/day (CV: 32%) and terminal elimination half-life was 17 days (95% CI: 15, 18 days).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In studies conducted in vitro in DLBCL tumor cells, tafasitamab-cxix in combination with lenalidomide resulted in increased ADCC activity compared to tafasitamab-cxix or lenalidomide alone.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: MONJUVI, in combination with lenalidomide, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) not otherwise specified, including DLBCL arising from low grade lymphoma, and who are not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Myelosuppression [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ] Infections [see Warnings and Precautions (5.3) ] The most common adverse reactions (≥20%) are neutropenia, fatigue, anemia, diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, cough, pyrexia, peripheral edema, respiratory tract infection, and decreased appetite.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on its mechanism of action, MONJUVI may cause fetal B-cell depletion when administered to a pregnant woman [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of tafasitamab-cxix in human milk or the effects on the breastfed child or milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Tafasitamab-cxix has a molecular weight of approximately 150 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Tafasitamab-cxix is an Fc-modified monoclonal antibody that binds to CD19 antigen expressed on the surface of pre-B and mature B lymphocytes and on several B-cell malignancies, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of MONJUVI in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate [see Clinical Studies (14) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upon binding to CD19, tafasitamab-cxix mediates B-cell lysis through apoptosis and immune effector mechanisms, including antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP).

Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies of MONJUVI did not include sufficient numbers of patients aged 65 and older to determine whether effectiveness differs compared to that of younger subjects.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The total volume of distribution for tafasitamab-cxix was 9.3 L (95% CI: 8.6, 10 L).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination The clearance of tafasitamab-cxix was 0.41 L/day (CV: 32%) and terminal elimination half-life was 17 days (95% CI: 15, 18 days).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In studies conducted in vitro in DLBCL tumor cells, tafasitamab-cxix in combination with lenalidomide resulted in increased ADCC activity compared to tafasitamab-cxix or lenalidomide alone.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: MONJUVI, in combination with lenalidomide, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) not otherwise specified, including DLBCL arising from low grade lymphoma, and who are not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Myelosuppression [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ] Infections [see Warnings and Precautions (5.3) ] The most common adverse reactions (≥20%) are neutropenia, fatigue, anemia, diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, cough, pyrexia, peripheral edema, respiratory tract infection, and decreased appetite.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on its mechanism of action, MONJUVI may cause fetal B-cell depletion when administered to a pregnant woman [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of tafasitamab-cxix in human milk or the effects on the breastfed child or milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Tafasitamab-cxix has a molecular weight of approximately 150 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Tafasitamab-cxix is an Fc-modified monoclonal antibody that binds to CD19 antigen expressed on the surface of pre-B and mature B lymphocytes and on several B-cell malignancies, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of MONJUVI in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate [see Clinical Studies (14) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Tafasitamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upon binding to CD19, tafasitamab-cxix mediates B-cell lysis through apoptosis and immune effector mechanisms, including antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP).

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 165 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma treated with TECVAYLI in MajesTEC-1 at the recommended dosage, 48% were 65 years of age or older, and 15% were 75 years of age or older.

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on the mechanism of action, TECVAYLI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant patient [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of teclistamab-cqyv in human milk, the effect on the breastfed child, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: TECVAYLI is a bispecific B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed CD3 T-cell engager indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma: in combination with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj in patients who have received at least one prior line of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent ( 1 ).

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Teclistamab-cqyv is a bispecific T-cell engaging antibody that binds to the CD3 receptor expressed on the surface of T-cells and B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) expressed on the surface of multiple myeloma cells and some healthy B-lineage cells.

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The molecular weight of teclistamab-cqyv is approximately 146 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and efficacy of TECVAYLI have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: WARNING: CYTOKINE RELEASE SYNDROME and NEUROLOGIC TOXICITY, including IMMUNE EFFECTOR CELL-ASSOCIATED NEUROTOXICITY SYNDROME Cytokine release syndrome (CRS), including life-threatening or fatal reactions, can occur in patients receiving TECVAYLI.

sourceReadings.label: Teclistamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: as monotherapy, in patients who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody ( 1 ).

Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 ) the adjuvant treatment of patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer who have residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane and trastuzumab-based treatment.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine is a HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Based on population pharmacokinetic analysis, the central volume of distribution of ADC was 3.13 L.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination Based on population pharmacokinetic analysis, following intravenous infusion of KADCYLA, the clearance of the ADC was 0.68 L/day and the elimination half-life (t 1/2 ) was approximately 4 days.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: If KADCYLA is administered during pregnancy, or if a patient becomes pregnant while receiving KADCYLA or within 7 months following the last dose of KADCYLA, health care providers and patients should immediately report KADCYLA exposure to Genentech at 1-888-835-2555.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In vitro, DM1 was a substrate of P-glycoprotein (P-gp).

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: KADCYLA is a HER2-targeted antibody and microtubule inhibitor conjugate indicated, as a single agent, for: the treatment of patients with HER2-positive, metastatic breast cancer who previously received trastuzumab and a taxane, separately or in combination.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Metabolism In vitro studies indicate that DM1, the small molecule component of KADCYLA, undergoes metabolism by CYP3A4/5.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No adjustment to the starting dose is required for patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dedicated renal impairment trial for KADCYLA has been conducted.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 495 patients who were randomized to KADCYLA in EMILIA [see Clinical Studies (14.1) ] , 65 patients (13%) were ≥ 65 years of age and 11 patients (2%) were ≥ 75 years of age.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Patients should have either: received prior therapy for metastatic disease, or developed disease recurrence during or within six months of completing adjuvant therapy.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There is no information regarding the presence of ado-trastuzumab emtansine in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Safety and effectiveness of KADCYLA have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The antibody is the humanized anti-HER2 IgG1, trastuzumab.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The small molecule cytotoxin, DM1, is a microtubule inhibitor.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upon binding to sub-domain IV of the HER2 receptor, ado-trastuzumab emtansine undergoes receptor-mediated internalization and subsequent lysosomal degradation, resulting in intracellular release of DM1-containing cytotoxic catabolites.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY, CARDIAC TOXICITY, EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY Hepatotoxicity: Serious hepatotoxicity has been reported, including liver failure and death in patients treated with KADCYLA.

sourceReadings.label: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: s and Precautions (5.7) ] Neurotoxicity [See Warnings and Precautions (5.8) ] Metastatic Breast Cancer The most common adverse reactions (≥ 25%) with KADCYLA were fatigue, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, hemorrhage, thrombocytopenia, headache, increased transaminases, constipation and epistaxis.

sourceReadings.label: Published labels naming Axatilimab as an active ingredient
Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Axatilimab-csfr has an approximate molecular weight of 150 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Axatilimab-csfr is a monoclonal antibody that binds to colony stimulating factor-1 receptors (CSF-1R) expressed on monocytes and macrophages.

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Blocking CSF-1R with axatilimab-csfr reduces the levels of these circulating proinflammatory and profibrotic monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages, as demonstrated by a reduction of nonclassical monocyte counts in nonclinical studies with axatilimab-csfr, and inhibits the activity of pathogenic macrophages in tissues.

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution Axatilimab-csfr volume of distribution is 6.06 L (16.3% CV).

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: NIKTIMVO is a colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R)-blocking antibody indicated for the treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg.

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: NIKTIMVO is indicated for the treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg.

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Of the 79 patients with cGVHD treated with NIKTIMVO, 21 (26.6%) were 65 years and older, and 2 (2.5%) were 75 years and older [see Clinical Studies ( 14 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on its mechanism of action, NIKTIMVO may cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant women [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.1 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of axatilimab-csfr in human milk or the effects on the breastfed child or milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The total clearance of axatilimab-csfr is composed of linear and non-linear components such that axatilimab-csfr clearance decreased from 2.32 mL/h/kg to 0.21 mL/h/kg and mean terminal half-life increased from 10.7 hours to 108 hours following single-dose administrations of axatilimab-csfr over a dose range of 0.15 mg/kg to 3 mg/kg (0.5 to 10 times the approved recommended dosage).

sourceReadings.label: Axatilimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Use of NIKTIMVO in pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg is supported by evidence from clinical trials that included 3 children (ages 6 to less than 12 years old) and 5 adolescents (ages 12 to less than 17 years old) [see Clinical Studies ( 14 )] .

sourceReadings.excerpt: Cipaglucosidase alfa-atga has a molecular weight of approximately 110 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Cipaglucosidase alfa-atga provides an exogenous source of GAA.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical trials of POMBILITI in combination with Opfolda did not include sufficient numbers of patients 65 years of age and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger adult patients.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination When cipaglucosidase alfa-atga was administered with Opfolda, the mean total body clearance (CL) of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga was 0.8 L/hour and the mean half-life of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga was 2.1 hours in ERT‑experienced patients.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: GAA deficiency results in intra-lysosomal accumulation of glycogen in various tissues.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: PK Parameter Cipaglucosidase alfa-atga 20 mg/kg in Combination with Opfolda 260 mg Cipaglucosidase alfa-atga 20 mg/kg † C max (mcg/mL) 345 (18.5) 325 (13.5) AUC 0-inf (mcg*h/mL) 1812 (20.8) 1410 (15.9) Distribution The volume of distribution of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga ranged from 2.0 to 4.7 L.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: POMBILITI is a hydrolytic lysosomal glycogen-specific enzyme indicated, in combination with Opfolda, an enzyme stabilizer, for the treatment of adult patients with late-onset Pompe disease (lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase [GAA] deficiency) weighing ≥40 kg and who are not improving on their current enzyme replacement therapy (ERT).

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: POMBILITI is indicated, in combination with Opfolda, for the treatment of adult patients with late-onset Pompe disease (lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase [GAA] deficiency) weighing ≥40 kg and who are not improving on their current enzyme replacement therapy (ERT).

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Pompe disease (also known as glycogen storage disease type II, acid maltase deficiency, and glycogenosis type II) is an inherited disorder of glycogen metabolism caused by a deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha‑glucosidase (GAA) that degrades glycogen to glucose in the lysosome.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on findings from animal reproduction studies, POMBILITI in combination with Opfolda may cause embryo-fetal harm when administered to a pregnant female and is contraindicated during pregnancy.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga, alone or in combination with miglustat, in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Safety and effectiveness of POMBILITI in combination with Opfolda have not been established in pediatric patients with late-onset Pompe disease.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The bis-M6P on cipaglucosidase alfa-atga mediates binding to M6P receptors on the cell surface with high affinity.

sourceReadings.label: Cipaglucosidase alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) reported in the pooled safety population of patients treated with POMBILITI in combination with Opfolda in the 3 clinical trials were headache, diarrhea, fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain and pyrexia.

sourceReadings.excerpt: CONTRAINDICATIONS RYZNEUTA is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious allergic reactions to granulocyte stimulating factors such as efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw, pegfilgrastim, or filgrastim products [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies of RYZNEUTA did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The geometric mean (CV%) apparent volume of distribution of efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw was 18.8 L (257%) in Cycle 1 and 40.7 L (387%) in Cycle 3 in female patients with breast cancer.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw is a colony-stimulating factor that acts on hematopoietic cells by binding to specific cell surface receptors, thereby stimulating proliferation, differentiation, commitment, and end cell functional activation.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: INDICATIONS AND USAGE RYZNEUTA is indicated to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Limitations of Use RYZNEUTA is not indicated for the mobilization of peripheral blood progenitor cells for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Patients with a history of serious allergic reactions to granulocyte stimulating factors such as efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw, pegfilgrastim, or filgrastim products.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: RYZNEUTA is a leukocyte growth factor indicated to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Although available data with RYZNEUTA use in pregnant women are insufficient to establish whether there is a drug associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes, there are available data from published studies in pregnant women exposed to other human G-CSF products.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw or its metabolite in either human or animal milk, the effects on the breastfed child, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The dimer is a water-soluble, glycosylated protein with a molecular weight of approximately 93.4 kilodaltons (kDa), of which 89.5 kDa is attributed to amino acids (protein sequence) and the remainder is from glycosylation.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim alfa label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The geometric mean (CV%) elimination half-life of efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw was 35.6 h (108%) in Cycle 1 and 36.9 h (120%) in Cycle 3.

Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: CONTRAINDICATIONS RYZNEUTA is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious allergic reactions to granulocyte stimulating factors such as efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw, pegfilgrastim, or filgrastim products [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )] .

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies of RYZNEUTA did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The geometric mean (CV%) apparent volume of distribution of efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw was 18.8 L (257%) in Cycle 1 and 40.7 L (387%) in Cycle 3 in female patients with breast cancer.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw is a colony-stimulating factor that acts on hematopoietic cells by binding to specific cell surface receptors, thereby stimulating proliferation, differentiation, commitment, and end cell functional activation.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: INDICATIONS AND USAGE RYZNEUTA is indicated to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Limitations of Use RYZNEUTA is not indicated for the mobilization of peripheral blood progenitor cells for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Patients with a history of serious allergic reactions to granulocyte stimulating factors such as efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw, pegfilgrastim, or filgrastim products.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: RYZNEUTA is a leukocyte growth factor indicated to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Although available data with RYZNEUTA use in pregnant women are insufficient to establish whether there is a drug associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes, there are available data from published studies in pregnant women exposed to other human G-CSF products.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are no data on the presence of efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw or its metabolite in either human or animal milk, the effects on the breastfed child, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Efbemalenograstim Alfa-Vuxw label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The dimer is a water-soluble, glycosylated protein with a molecular weight of approximately 93.4 kilodaltons (kDa), of which 89.5 kDa is attributed to amino acids (protein sequence) and the remainder is from glycosylation.

sourceReadings.label: Published labels naming Epcoritamab as an active ingredient
Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 ) This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution The apparent total volume of distribution is 25.6 L (82%).

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: EPKINLY is a bispecific CD20-directed CD3 T-cell engager indicated: For the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified, including DLBCL arising from indolent lymphoma, and high-grade B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines of systemic therapy.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination The half-life of full dose epcoritamab-bysp (48 mg) was approximately 22 days (58%) at the end of Cycle 3, with apparent total clearance of approximately 0.53 L/day (40%) after the end of Cycle 3.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Epcoritamab-bysp is a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody that binds to the CD3 receptor expressed on the surface of T-cells and CD20 expressed on the surface of lymphoma cells and healthy B-lineage cells.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Epcoritamab-bysp is manufactured in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells using recombinant DNA technology and has an approximate molecular weight of 149 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In nonclinical studies, the combination of epcoritamab-bysp and rituximab resulted in both T-cell mediated cytotoxicity and natural killer (NK) cell mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In vitro, epcoritamab-bysp activated T-cells, caused the release of proinflammatory cytokines, and induced lysis of B-cells.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: LBCL In patients with relapsed or refractory LBCL who received EPKINLY in EPCORE NHL-1, 77 (49%) were 65 years of age and older, and 29 (19%) were 75 years of age or older.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on the mechanism of action, EPKINLY may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There is no information regarding the presence of epcoritamab-bysp in human milk, the effect on the breastfed child, or milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and efficacy of EPKINLY in pediatric patients have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Epcoritamab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: WARNING: CYTOKINE RELEASE SYNDROME AND IMMUNE EFFECTOR CELL-ASSOCIATED NEUROTOXICITY SYNDROME Cytokine release syndrome (CRS), including serious or fatal reactions, can occur in patients receiving EPKINLY.

sourceReadings.label: Published labels naming Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki as an active ingredient
Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label naming this substance alone
Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 ) HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer in combination with pertuzumab as first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+) breast cancer, as determined by an FDA-authorized test.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ( 1.1 ) as adjuvant treatment of adult patients with HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+) breast cancer who have residual invasive disease following neoadjuvant trastuzumab (with or without pertuzumab) and taxane-based treatment.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: DXd is a substrate of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE2-K, P-gp, MRP1, and BCRP.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: DXd is a substrate of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE2-K, P-gp, MRP1, and BCRP. 12.6 Immunogenicity The observed incidence of anti-drug antibodies (ADA) is highly dependent on the sensitivity and specificity of the assay.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: DXd is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: DXd plasma protein binding is approximately 97% and the blood-to-plasma ratio is approximately 0.6 in vitro.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Drug Interaction Studies Clinical Studies No clinically significant differences in pharmacokinetics of fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki or DXd were observed when used concomitantly with itraconazole (strong CYP3A inhibitor) or ritonavir (strong CYP3A inhibitor and OATP inhibitor).

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ENHERTU as Monotherapy Of the 2233 patients treated with ENHERTU 5.4 mg/kg, 28% were 65 years or older and 6% were 75 years or older.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ENHERTU is a HER2-directed antibody and topoisomerase inhibitor conjugate indicated for: HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer as neoadjuvant treatment of adult patients with HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+) Stage II or III breast cancer, as determined by an FDA-authorized test followed by a taxane, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP).

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Elimination The median elimination half-life of fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki is 5.4 to 5.7 days.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki is a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Following binding to HER2 on tumor cells, fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki undergoes internalization and intracellular linker cleavage by lysosomal enzymes.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In Vitro Studies CYP450 Enzymes : DXd does not inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A nor induce CYP1A2, CYP2B6, or CYP3A.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dose adjustment of ENHERTU is recommended in patients with mild (creatinine clearance [CLcr] 60 to <90 mL/min) or moderate (CLcr 30 to <60 mL/min) renal impairment [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: No dose adjustment of ENHERTU is recommended in patients with mild (total bilirubin ≤ULN and any AST >ULN or total bilirubin >1 to 1.5 times ULN and any AST) or moderate (total bilirubin >1.5 to 3 times ULN and any AST) hepatic impairment.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Based on its mechanism of action, ENHERTU can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There is no data regarding the presence of fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki in human milk, the effects on the breastfed child, or the effects on milk production.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Safety and effectiveness of ENHERTU have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The antibody is a humanized anti-HER2 IgG1.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The small molecule, DXd, is a topoisomerase I inhibitor attached to the antibody by a cleavable linker.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Transporter Systems : DXd is not an inhibitor of OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1, MATE2-K, P-gp, BCRP, or BSEP.

sourceReadings.label: Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki label
sourceReadings.excerpt: WARNING: INTERSTITIAL LUNG DISEASE and EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) and pneumonitis, including severe, life-threatening, and fatal cases, have been reported with ENHERTU.

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: 11 DESCRIPTION Nemolizumab-ilto, an interleukin-31 receptor alpha (IL-31RA) antagonist, is a humanized monoclonal modified immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody with a molecular weight of approximately 144 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical trials of NEMLUVIO did not include sufficient numbers of subjects 65 years of age or older to determine whether they respond differently than younger adult subjects. [ see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ].

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label

sourceReadings.excerpt: Known hypersensitivity to nemolizumab-ilto or to any of the excipients in NEMLUVIO.

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: NEMLUVIO is contraindicated in patients who have known hypersensitivity to nemolizumab-ilto or to any of the excipients in NEMLUVIO [ see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ].

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Nemolizumab-ilto inhibited IL-31-induced responses including the release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines.

sourceReadings.label: Nemolizumab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Prurigo Nodularis The safety and effectiveness of NEMLUVIO have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Available data on NEMLUVIO use in pregnant women exposed during clinical trials are insufficient to evaluate for a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies of IMAAVY did not include sufficient numbers of patients aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently from younger adult patients.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Distribution Mean volume of distribution of nipocalimab-aahu is 2.67 L.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: IMAAVY is a neonatal Fc receptor blocker indicated for the treatment of: generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody positive.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: IMAAVY is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reaction to nipocalimab-aahu or any of the excipients in IMAAVY.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: IMAAVY is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reaction to nipocalimab-aahu or to any of the excipients in IMAAVY.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Nipocalimab-aahu has an approximate molecular weight of 142 kilodaltons (kDa).

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Nipocalimab-aahu is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds to neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), resulting in the reduction of circulating IgG levels.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Reactions have included anaphylaxis and angioedema [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ] .

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary Nipocalimab-aahu is excreted in human colostrum and breastmilk based on limited data from an investigational study of 13 pregnant women administered nipocalimab-aahu during pregnancy where colostrum and breastmilk was assessed in the first 8 days after birth.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Risk Summary There are limited data on the use of IMAAVY in pregnant women to inform a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: gMG The safety and effectiveness of IMAAVY for the treatment of gMG have been established in pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.

sourceReadings.label: Nipocalimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: sitivity Reactions [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ] Infusion-related Reactions [see Warnings and Precautions (5.3) ] The most common adverse reactions (≥10%) in patients with gMG treated with IMAAVY were respiratory tract infections, peripheral edema, and muscle spasms.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Binding of the PD-1 ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, to the PD-1 receptor found on T cells, inhibits T-cell proliferation and cytokine production.

sourceReadings.label: Retifanlimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Clinical studies of ZYNYZ as a single agent did not include sufficient numbers of younger adult patients to determine if patients 65 years of age and older respond differently than younger adult patients.

sourceReadings.label: Retifanlimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Retifanlimab-dlwr binds to the PD-1 receptor, blocks interaction with its ligands PD-L1 and PD‑L2, and potentiates T-cell activity.

sourceReadings.label: Retifanlimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Retifanlimab-dlwr has an approximate molecular weight of 148 kDa.

sourceReadings.label: Retifanlimab label

sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of ZYNYZ have not been established in pediatric patients.

sourceReadings.label: Retifanlimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upregulation of PD-1 ligands occurs in some tumors, and signaling through this pathway can contribute to inhibition of active T-cell immune surveillance of tumors.

sourceReadings.label: Retifanlimab label
sourceReadings.excerpt: ZYNYZ is a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1)–blocking antibody indicated: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Anal Canal (SCAC) in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel for the first-line treatment of adult patients with inoperable locally recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC).
